title: I Used the Co-op Shift Swap Board on the Member Who Never Worked

parts.text: I showed up for the 6 a.m. receiving shift at 5:58 and found the swap board had my name in ink and hers in pencil for a shift she had not worked since April. The member, Sasha, still had a full discount. I was forty-three, produce, holding a time card. The board rules said ink is the work. I photographed ink, pencil, and the discount roster. Then I asked the membership coordinator to audit April–now. At 6:09 Sasha arrived with coffee for herself and said she would supervise.
parts.cliffhanger_hint: She arrived with coffee to supervise a shift that was penciled over my ink.

social.video_title: Ink versus pencil on the 6 a.m. receiving board — Part 1/2
social.description: Full discount, April gap, coffee for one. Audit requested. Would you have let her supervise?

parts.text: Membership froze the discount until hours landed. Sasha stocked. Pencil erased. Ink stood. I received the trucks. Coffee later became a pot, which is how co-ops survive. Supervising is a job they would have to elect. They did not. April got a repayment in hours. The board is honest at 5:58 now. Discounts follow sweat. I keep a pen on a string so pencil is a choice, not a fog.

social.video_title: The discount froze until the hours thawed — Part 2/2
social.description: Stocking, pot of coffee, pen on a string. Was supervising a shift?
